recognize_zh: 深色皮膚病人背部廣泛分布紫褐色斑疹，中央融合成片並伴有細碎鱗屑脫落，邊緣呈斑駁點狀；在深色皮膚上急性 GVHD 的紅斑常呈紫褐色或色素沉著，而非鮮紅色。
features: Widespread violaceous to dark brown macules and patches over the entire back and flanks
Central confluence with fine to plate-like scaling and superficial desquamation
Mottled, discrete macules at the periphery merging toward the center
Erythema appears violaceous/hyperpigmented on darkly pigmented skin
No bullae, sclerosis or deep ulceration visible
describe_en: Clinical photograph of the back in a patient with darkly pigmented skin shows an extensive eruption of violaceous-brown macules and patches that coalesce centrally, with overlying fine scale and areas of superficial desquamation; the periphery shows discrete, mottled macules. No blisters, sclerotic plaques or ulcers are evident. In the post-transplant setting, this extensive desquamating eruption is consistent with cutaneous acute graft-versus-host disease, with hyperpigmentation reflecting skin of color or evolving post-inflammatory change; lichenoid chronic GVHD and drug eruption should be excluded clinically and histologically.

ddx.vs: Chronic lichenoid GVHD forms flat-topped violaceous papules and plaques with hyperkeratosis and later sclerosis rather than a diffuse desquamating macular eruption.

ddx.dx: Drug reaction (DRESS or exfoliative drug eruption)
ddx.vs: DRESS shows facial edema, eosinophilia and organ involvement after a latency of weeks following a culprit drug.
Requires a prior dermatologic history; histology shows psoriasiform or spongiotic change without basal apoptotic keratinocytes.
